## Overview

::: {.callout-important}
## Focus for Today
This session focuses on **running your study and managing data collection**. By the end, you should:

- Begin or continue data collection
- Conduct quality checks on incoming data
- Troubleshoot common problems
- Complete initial data review
:::

---

## Activity 1: Running Your Study (20 min)

### Pre-Session Checklist

Before each data collection session, verify:

- [ ] All materials ready
- [ ] Technology tested (if applicable)
- [ ] Quiet space secured
- [ ] Consent forms available
- [ ] Data recording system working

**True or False: You should test your equipment EVERY time before collecting data.** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

### Experimenter Behaviour

::: {.callout-warning}
## Avoiding Experimenter Bias
Your behaviour can influence participant responses. Stay neutral and consistent.
:::

**Which experimenter behaviour could bias results?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Reading standardised instructions</option><option value=''>Maintaining a neutral expression</option><option value='answer'>Nodding encouragingly when participants give certain answers</option><option value=''>Following the same procedure with everyone</option></select>

**The term for participants behaving differently because they know they're being studied is:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Confirmation bias</option><option value='answer'>Hawthorne effect</option><option value=''>Selection bias</option><option value=''>Observer effect</option></select>

### Handling Questions

During data collection, participants may ask questions. How should you respond?

**A participant asks: "What answer are you looking for?"**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Tell them the hypothesis</option><option value=''>Hint at the 'correct' answer</option><option value='answer'>Explain there are no right or wrong answers and to respond honestly</option><option value=''>End the session</option></select>

**A participant seems distressed during the study. You should:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Ignore it and continue</option><option value=''>Force them to complete the study</option><option value='answer'>Check in, remind them they can stop, and offer support resources</option><option value=''>Pretend not to notice</option></select>

**True or False: Participants can skip questions they don't want to answer.** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

---

## Activity 2: Quality Checks (20 min)

### Real-Time Data Monitoring

Check your data as it comes in:

::: {.callout-note}
## Quality Check Indicators
- Response rates (how many completing vs starting)
- Completion times (too fast = not reading; too slow = distracted?)
- Missing data patterns
- Response distributions (all same answer = problematic)
:::

**If a participant completes a 15-minute survey in 2 minutes, you should:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Include their data - they're just fast</option><option value='answer'>Flag for review - they likely didn't read questions properly</option><option value=''>Immediately delete their data</option><option value=''>Ask them to redo it</option></select>

### Attention Checks

Many studies include attention check questions:

> "For this question, please select 'Strongly Agree'"

**The purpose of attention checks is to:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Trick participants</option><option value='answer'>Identify participants who aren't reading questions</option><option value=''>Make the survey longer</option><option value=''>Test intelligence</option></select>

**If a participant fails an attention check, you should:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Always include their data</option><option value=''>Always exclude their data</option><option value='answer'>Follow your pre-registered exclusion criteria</option><option value=''>Ask them to explain themselves</option></select>

### Missing Data

**True or False: Some missing data is normal and expected.** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

**What pattern of missing data is MOST concerning?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Random items missing across participants</option><option value='answer'>All participants skipping the same question</option><option value=''>One participant missing one item</option><option value=''>Different participants missing different items</option></select>

**If all participants skip question 7, this suggests:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Question 7 is fine</option><option value='answer'>Question 7 may be confusing, sensitive, or have a technical problem</option><option value=''>Your sample is too small</option><option value=''>You need more attention checks</option></select>

---

## Activity 3: Troubleshooting (20 min)

### Common Problems and Solutions

Work through these scenarios:

**Problem: Recruitment is slower than expected**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Give up and use whatever data you have</option><option value='answer'>Expand recruitment methods, extend timeline, or adjust sample size expectations</option><option value=''>Make up additional data</option><option value=''>Reduce your standards for who can participate</option></select>

**Problem: A participant tells others about the study (including the manipulation)**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>It doesn't matter</option><option value='answer'>Note this, recruit from different pools if possible, assess potential contamination</option><option value=''>Confront the participant</option><option value=''>Cancel the entire study</option></select>

**Problem: Technology fails mid-session**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Pretend it didn't happen</option><option value=''>Force the participant to wait indefinitely</option><option value='answer'>Apologise, note the incident, restart if possible or reschedule</option><option value=''>Blame the participant</option></select>

### Ethical Issues During Collection

**A participant reveals something concerning (e.g., self-harm) during the study:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Ignore it - you're not a therapist</option><option value=''>Include it in your data write-up</option><option value='answer'>Pause, express concern, provide support resources, consider whether to continue</option><option value=''>End the study immediately without explanation</option></select>

**True or False: You should have a plan for handling distressed participants BEFORE data collection begins.** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

### Documentation

Keep a log of any issues:

| Date | Participant | Issue | Resolution |
|------|-------------|-------|------------|
| | | | |
| | | | |
| | | | |

**Why is documentation important?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>It's not really important</option><option value='answer'>It helps explain anomalies and improves future studies</option><option value=''>Only for ethics audits</option><option value=''>To blame others for problems</option></select>

---

## Activity 4: Initial Data Review (20 min)

### First Look at Your Data

Before formal analysis, do a quick review:

::: {.callout-note}
## Initial Review Checklist
1. How many responses so far?
2. Any obvious data entry errors?
3. Are all conditions represented?
4. Are responses in expected ranges?
5. Any patterns in missing data?
:::

### Checking Distributions

**If you asked for age and someone entered "999", this is:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>A valid response</option><option value='answer'>Likely an error requiring correction or exclusion</option><option value=''>Evidence of immortality</option><option value=''>Fine to include in your mean</option></select>

**Before calculating means, you should:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Just calculate them immediately</option><option value='answer'>Check for outliers and impossible values</option><option value=''>Delete any values you don't like</option><option value=''>Assume everything is correct</option></select>

### Sample Characteristics

Check your sample composition:

**If your study is about "adults in general" but your sample is 95% female psychology students aged 18-22:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>This is perfectly representative</option><option value='answer'>This limits generalisability and should be noted as a limitation</option><option value=''>This means the study is invalid</option><option value=''>Gender and age don't matter</option></select>

**True or False: You should report your sample demographics in your Methods section.** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

### Pre-Analysis Plan Review

Before analysing, confirm:

1. **Primary hypothesis**: ___
2. **Planned analysis**: ___
3. **Exclusion criteria**: ___
4. **Minimum sample size**: ___

**When should exclusion criteria be decided?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>After seeing the data</option><option value='answer'>Before data collection (ideally pre-registered)</option><option value=''>During analysis</option><option value=''>When writing up results</option></select>

**On track?** <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Yes - ahead of schedule</option><option value=''>Yes - on track</option><option value='answer'>Need to assess as a group</option><option value=''>No - behind schedule</option></select>

---

## Group Discussion: Status Update

Discuss as a group:

1. **Recruitment progress**: Are you on track?
2. **Procedure issues**: Any problems running the study?
3. **Data quality**: Any concerns with responses?
4. **Team coordination**: Is everyone contributing?
5. **Timeline**: Realistic for completion?

---

## Key Takeaways

::: {.callout-important}
## Summary

1. **Consistent procedure** is essential - follow your protocol exactly
2. **Quality checks** should happen throughout data collection, not just at the end
3. **Document problems** to help explain your data and improve future studies
4. **Initial data review** helps catch issues before formal analysis
:::

---

## Next Steps

- Hand all data sheets to Gordon at the end of today's session
- Gordon will analyse the data over Easter and return it in Week 20
- Start thinking about your Research Report structure
- Prepare for the Report Writing Workshop (Week 20)

## Data Collection Ends Today
All data collection must be complete by the end of today's lab session. Hand your data to Gordon — he will analyse it and return your results in Week 20.
